nodes.label: Ten non-negotiable animation standards
nodes.rationale: Justified motion, frequency-appropriate motion, responsive easing, sub-300ms UI, origin and physical correctness, interruptibility, GPU-only properties, accessibility, asymmetric enter and exit, and cohesion. Default is to flag; approval is earned, because motion that merely runs but feels sluggish or lands from the wrong origin is a regression.

nodes.label: Aggressive escalation triggers
nodes.rationale: Flagged on sight: transition: all, scale(0) entrances, ease-in on UI, animation on keyboard or 100+/day actions, over-300ms UI durations, centered origin on anchored popovers, keyframes on rapidly-triggered elements, layout-property animation, parent CSS variables driving child transforms, missing reduced motion, ungated hover, symmetric press timing, and everything entering at once.

nodes.label: Remedial preference hierarchy
nodes.rationale: Fixes are proposed in order: delete the animation, reduce it, fix the easing, fix the origin and physicality, make it interruptible, move it to the GPU, make the timing asymmetric, polish, then accessibility and cohesion. Deleting comes first because when motion's rightness is uncertain the strongest move is often removal.

nodes.label: Emil Kowalski's animation philosophy
nodes.rationale: The substantive craft bar (animations.dev) shared by the build, audit and review skills, so an animation written by one passes the review of another. The review method itself is adapted separately from aggressive code-quality review.
